pr_title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Improve logic for serving devices erase capabilities
pr_body:
The commit fixes issue where flash_area_flatten has been used where code was only supposed to erase devices by hardware requirement prior to write, by replacing the call with flash_area_erase and supporting logic to select proper path.
There have been following Kconfig options added:
 - CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_IO_FLASH_WITHOUT_ERASE
 - CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_IO_FLASH_WITH_ERASE
that are available for user depending on devices in the system and allow to turn off paths that are not used by BLOB IO; for example if user never writes to device with erase CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_IO_FLASH_WITH_ERASE will disable the path.
Both Kconfig options are y by default and enable all paths.

issue_context.title: bl_mesh_blob_io_flash: Probable issue with block_start logic and dependency on CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
In code here:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/3c42daee9c1b1898bbbdbaab1f32087339f5fd8c/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/blob_io_flash.c#L59-L93

We can see two issues:
 1) Setting of other subsystem, CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT, indirectly controls the code here
 2) Something that seems to be verification, and alignment, of parameters passed to flash_area_erase may be completely turned off by the Kconfig in other subsystem.

The 1) should probably be resolved by some `CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_` that would default to Y,  when `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y`, or by enforcing the dependency, on the unit that `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y`, always.
The existence of local `CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_`  to control the behaviour should describe that now blocks passed to `block_start` should be aligned to erase block of a device the `block_start` operates on (*).

Note that when `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y` then the code will correct erase size to align it with device requirements, and this reduces chances of `flash_area_erase` to fail, but also means that when passing `block->size` unaligned, to erase block of a device,  will work with  `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y` and fail when `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=n`: it seems that `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=n`, from other subsystem, controls correction of a parameter that is passed to other subsystem (seemingly unrelated).

Assuming that the said block->size is passed, when `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=n` top to bottom correct with the device layout, this means that the parameter has been checked somewhere before the call to `block_start` has been invoked. This means that the size alignment done at line 86, and entire 70-87 block, may not be needed at all.
If that is not the case, this probably means that unverified parameter has probably reached too low into a call path.

I do not think it should be allowed for the `flash_area_erase` to fail here due to incorrect `block->size` so the `CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y` is mandatory, which means that there is only one path in code and the #else could be removed.
comments: I do not think it is Flash, it is rather Bluetooth/Mash. I do not think I can fix it correctly without opinion from people who know how this is used, maintainers and so on.

review_comments: Hi @de-nordic, could you elaborate how is it possible to have both `CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_IO_FLASH_WITH_ERASE` and `CONFIG_BT_MESH_BLOB_IO_FLASH_WITHOUT_ERASE` at the same time?

I look at it from the point of the Flash API, not BT, so if I miss the point that this can not have different instances working on different devices, then you can correct me here.

You can have Flash API devices that support/require and do not support/require erase, but neither Flash API nor this subsystems have a way to figure out on which kind of device the this, the blob io, will be working.

For example you may have SoC with Flash but the blob io will work with external RRAM device; now only thing you know at this point, is that you have two kind of devices in your system: some with erase before write requirement and some without one.
So, by default both paths are here enabled, because it is impossible to figure out which one will be taken, but if you exactly know that you only use RRAM, then you do not require all the additional operations required by Flash and may remove them by disabling the path.
On the other side, if you are willing to run the blob on either of the devices, you may want to keep both paths enabled.
Ok, got it. Thanks for elaboration.
In which `system`? How is it related to ble mesh?
System as a set of features/drivers enabled in Zephyr running on a hardware.
